B291: Batch is a preserving cookbook by Joel MacCharles and Dana Harrison, the Canadian couple behind the Well Preserved blog. It collects small-batch recipes for jams, pickles, ferments, and sauces, organized around cooking and canning in modest quantities at home.
B240: Classic French Recipes is a translated edition of Ginette Mathiot's long-running French home-cooking collection. It gathers traditional dishes from soups and sauces to meat, fish, vegetables, and desserts, with short, practical instructions for everyday cooks.
B248: Dinner in an Instant is a pressure cooker cookbook by Melissa Clark, a New York Times food writer. It adapts weeknight dishes, soups, braises, grains, and desserts for the electric multicooker, with recipes built around speed and common ingredients.
B289: Genius Recipes is a collection by Kristen Miglore, drawn from her Food52 column of the same name. Each recipe comes from a notable cook or chef and includes a technique or shortcut that changes how a familiar dish is made.
B055: Heat is a memoir by New Yorker writer Bill Buford about leaving his editing job to work in the kitchen of Mario Batali's Babbo restaurant in New York. It follows his apprenticeships in Italy, including studies in pasta making and butchery with Italian masters.
B297: Indian(-ish) is a cookbook by Priya Krishna built around the home cooking of her mother, Ritu, in Dallas, Texas. The recipes blend Indian flavors with American ingredients and family improvisation, and the book includes stories from the Krishna household.
B293: My Bombay Kitchen presents the traditional home cooking of the Parsi community of Bombay, written by Niloufer Ichaporia King, an anthropologist and cook who divides her time between India and California. It mixes recipes, family history, and notes on Parsi customs, ingredients, and festivals.
B286: Speaking in Cod Tongues is a Canadian culinary travelogue by Lenore Newman, a geographer who studies food. She crosses Canada from coast to coast to examine the country's regional dishes and food traditions, and asks what a national cuisine might include.
B298: The Hot Bread Kitchen Cookbook collects recipes from the New York bakery of the same name, founded by Jessamyn Waldman Rodriguez. The bakery trains women from immigrant communities as bakers, and the book covers breads from many cultures along with the stories behind them.
B247: The Wurst! is a short illustrated guide to German food by Melbourne-based writer and cook Otto Wolff. It offers recipes for sausages, schnitzel, pretzels, potato salads, cakes, and other German staples, alongside notes on regional specialties.
B216: A Sentimental Journey Through France and Italy is an unfinished comic travel novel by Laurence Sterne, published in 1768. Its narrator, the clergyman Yorick, records small encounters and feelings on his trip, in a book written after Sterne's Tristram Shandy.
B072: Am Hang is a German-language novel by the Swiss writer Markus Werner, published in 1985. Two men meet at a hotel terrace in the mountains and talk about love, failure, and their lives, and the conversation shapes the course of the novel.
B145: Dead Air is a novel by Iain Banks, published in 2002 and set in London after the attacks of September 2001. Its narrator is a loud, opinionated radio shock jock whose life becomes tangled in a series of personal and criminal troubles.
B257: Ein Sommer in Niendorf is a 2022 German-language comic novel by Heinz Strunk. A 51-year-old Hamburg business lawyer rents a seaside apartment on the Baltic coast to write his family's history, and the summer brings encounters with other holidaymakers and locals.
B086: Heimatmuseum is a 1978 German novel by Siegfried Lenz, set in Masuria in what was then East Prussia. Its narrator tells the history of his family and region, and the fate of his local museum, against the backdrop of the Nazi era and its aftermath.
B126: How to Be Good is a 2001 novel by Nick Hornby, narrated by Katie Carr, a doctor in North London. Her marriage is strained when her sarcastic husband undergoes a sudden change of character, which prompts her to question her own ideas of what it means to be a good person.
B315: Kay's Lucky Coin Variety is a novel by the Toronto-based writer Ann Y. K. Choi. It follows a Korean-Canadian family connected to a small corner store, and covers themes of immigration, family, and daily life in Toronto.
B082: Neue Vahr Süd is a 2004 German novel by Sven Regener, set in Bremen in 1981. Its protagonist, Frank Lehmann, turns 20, serves in the army, and moves in a shared flat, in a story that forms part of the series about the character that also includes Herr Lehmann.
B231: Surfacing is a 1972 novel by the Canadian writer Margaret Atwood. An unnamed narrator travels with her boyfriend and two friends to a remote island in northern Quebec to search for her missing father, and the trip leads her to confront her past.
B147: The Business is a 1999 novel by Iain Banks about Kellie Peters, a senior executive at the Caledonian Highland Company, a secretive family-run global enterprise. When the firm considers seeking a seat in the United Nations, she is drawn into its plans and her own personal choices.
B274: The Kite Runner is a 2003 debut novel by Khaled Hosseini. It follows Amir, a boy from Kabul, his friendship with Hassan, the son of his father's servant, and the guilt that draws him back to Afghanistan years later after emigrating to the United States.
B029: The Mysterious Flame of Queen Loana is a 2004 illustrated novel by Umberto Eco. A Milan antiquarian bookseller who has lost his autobiographical memory after a stroke returns to his family home in the countryside and searches through old books, comics, records, and papers to recover his past.
B307: The Shipping News is a 1993 novel by E. Annie Proulx, set largely in Newfoundland. Quoyle, a struggling newspaper reporter from New York, moves with his daughters to his ancestral home on the island and takes a job covering the shipping news for a local paper.
B063: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle is a 1994 to 1995 novel by Haruki Murakami, set in Tokyo. An unemployed man searches for his missing cat and then his missing wife, and meets a cast of unusual characters while the story moves between modern Japan and wartime Manchuria.
B295: Bad Monkey is a 2013 comic crime novel by Carl Hiaasen, set in the Florida Keys and the Bahamas. A demoted police detective turned restaurant inspector investigates a severed arm found by a fishing tourist, and the case leads to a trail of corrupt developers and voodoo.
B140: Casino Royale is the first James Bond novel by Ian Fleming, published in 1953. British agent Bond is sent to a French casino to bankrupt Le Chiffre, a paymaster for a Soviet-linked union, in a high-stakes game of baccarat.
B102: Das Russlandhaus is the German edition of The Russia House, a 1989 Cold War spy novel by John le Carré. Barley Blair, a British publisher in Moscow, becomes the link for a Soviet scientist's manuscript on military secrets, and British and American intelligence services take an interest.
B275: Faceless Killers is the first Kurt Wallander novel by the Swedish author Henning Mankell, published in 1991. Inspector Wallander investigates the brutal murder of an elderly farming couple in southern Sweden, and the case stirs up local tension about immigration.
B181: From Russia with Love is the fifth James Bond novel by Ian Fleming, published in 1957. Soviet counterintelligence plans to discredit and kill Bond through a trap involving a Soviet cipher clerk, and the plot leads him to Istanbul and the Orient Express.
B254: LaBrava is a 1983 crime novel by Elmore Leonard, set in Miami Beach. Joe LaBrava, a former Secret Service agent working as a photographer, meets a faded film actress and becomes entangled in a blackmail and kidnapping plot.
B044: One Fine Day in the Middle of the Night is a 1999 comic thriller by the Scottish writer Christopher Brookmyre. A school reunion held on a converted North Sea oil rig turns into a hostage crisis when armed mercenaries arrive, and a few former classmates try to rescue the others.
B165: Restless is a 2006 spy novel by William Boyd. A young woman in 1970s England learns that her mother was a British agent during the Second World War, and she reads her mother's account of her recruitment and work.
B228: Slow Horses is the first novel in Mick Herron's Slough House series, published in 2010. It follows a group of disgraced MI5 officers exiled to a run-down office, who become involved in the kidnapping of a young British Pakistani man.
B050: The Blood of Angels is a 2005 thriller by Michael Marshall, the third book to feature Ward Hopkins and the group known as the Straw Men. Ward is drawn back into a search for answers about a serial killer network and his own past.
B219: The Ethical Assassin is a 2006 comic thriller by David Liss, set in Florida in 1980. A teenage encyclopedia salesman knocks on the wrong door and meets a hit man who follows a personal code of ethics, which draws him into a chain of killings.
B009: The Girl Who Played with Fire is the second novel in Stieg Larsson's Millennium series, published in 2006. Lisbeth Salander becomes the prime suspect in a triple murder, and the journalist Mikael Blomkvist investigates to clear her name.
B092: The Return of Sherlock Holmes is a 1905 collection of 13 short stories by Arthur Conan Doyle. It brings the detective back after his apparent death at Reichenbach Falls, and includes cases such as The Adventure of the Dancing Men and The Adventure of the Six Napoleons.
B217: Three Bags Full is a 2005 mystery by the German author Leonie Swann, subtitled A Sheep Detective Story. A flock of sheep in Ireland sets out to find out who killed their shepherd, using their own observations and limited knowledge of human behavior.
B125: Consider Phlebas is the first Culture novel by Iain M. Banks, published in 1987. Horza, a shapeshifting mercenary who sides with the Idirans, is sent on a mission during the war between the Idirans and the Culture, a post-scarcity civilization run by artificial minds.
B026: Hyperion is a 1989 science fiction novel by Dan Simmons, the first of the Hyperion Cantos. Seven pilgrims travel to the Time Tombs on a distant world, where the Shrike waits, and each tells a story of how they came to make the journey.
B040: Snow Crash is a 1992 science fiction novel by Neal Stephenson. Hiro Protagonist, a pizza deliverer and hacker in a near-future America of franchise territories, investigates a computer virus in the virtual Metaverse that also affects people in the physical world.
B321: Use of Weapons is a 1990 Culture novel by Iain M. Banks. Its chapters alternate between the current mission of Cheradenine Zakalwe, a mercenary employed by the Culture, and episodes from his earlier life that run in reverse order.
B324: Fool is a 2009 comic retelling of Shakespeare's King Lear by Christopher Moore. The story follows Pocket, the king's jester, who narrates events in a bawdy voice as Lear's daughters scheme for power in a fictional Britain.
B259: Mexican Gothic is a 2020 horror novel by Silvia Moreno-Garcia, set in 1950s Mexico. Noemí Taboada, a young socialite, travels to a remote mountain mansion to check on her newly married cousin, and finds a decaying house and a secretive English family.
B068: Tailchaser's Song is the 1985 debut novel by Tad Williams. Fritti Tailchaser, a young tomcat, leaves his home to search for a missing friend, and his travels bring him into the secret world of cat society, myths, and dangers.
B326: The Return of the King is the third volume of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, published in 1955. The war against Sauron reaches its climax at Minas Tirith and the Black Gate, while Frodo and Sam make their way into Mordor to destroy the Ring.
B041: Whitechapel Gods is a 2008 steampunk novel by S. M. Peters, set in a walled-off district of Victorian London ruled by two machine gods. A resistance group of outcasts inside the district tries to overthrow them.
B196: Birdsong is a 1993 novel by Sebastian Faulks that moves between 1910 and the 1970s. It follows Stephen Wraysford, an English officer on the Western Front in the First World War, and a later descendant who researches his story.
B073: Die Säulen der Erde is the German edition of Ken Follett's The Pillars of the Earth, a 1989 historical novel. It follows the building of a cathedral in the fictional English town of Kingsbridge during the 12th century, and the civil war known as the Anarchy.
B322: Half-Blood Blues is a 2011 novel by the Canadian author Esi Edugyan. It follows a group of jazz musicians in Berlin and Paris in 1939 and 1940, including a young Black German trumpeter who vanishes, and their later lives in the 1990s.
B317: My Name Is Red is a 1998 novel by the Turkish writer Orhan Pamuk, set in Istanbul in 1591. A murder among the Ottoman court miniaturists drives the plot, and the chapters are told by multiple narrators, including the dead man, a corpse, and a coin.
B226: The Samurai Detective, Vol. 1 is a translated historical fiction collection by the Japanese novelist Shotaro Ikenami, set in the Edo period. It follows a samurai who investigates crimes and mysteries, in a series Ikenami wrote between 1972 and 1989.
B101: Die allerneueste klassische Sau is a German-language humor anthology, edited by Hermann Kinder, that collects erotic passages from classic literature. It belongs to a series that gathers suggestive and bawdy scenes from well-known writers.
B012: Sh*t My Dad Says is a 2010 humor book by Justin Halpern, based on his popular Twitter account. It collects blunt and profane remarks by his father, Sam Halpern, a retired nephrologist in San Diego, with commentary from the author.
B194: The Bones of Ruin is a 2018 young adult fantasy novel by the Canadian author Sarah Raughley. Iyanu, a young woman who cannot die, is taken into a Victorian-era circus act and then to a mysterious society that explains her past.
B214: The Prairie Dog Conspiracy is a young readers' mystery by the Canadian author Eric Wilson, part of his Tom and Liz Austen series. The two young detectives investigate a puzzling crime in the Canadian prairies.
B069: Das Profil der Mörder is the German edition of The Jigsaw Man by Paul Britton, a British forensic psychologist. He describes his work in offender profiling and the investigation of serial killings and other violent crimes in Britain.
B210: Londoners is a 2011 oral history by Craig Taylor, built from interviews with people who live and work in London. The speakers include a cab driver, a banker, an immigrant, and a street cleaner, and they describe the city and how it changes.
B191: The Farfarers is a 2012 history by Farley Mowat, the Canadian author, on the peoples who lived in the Arctic before the Vikings. It argues that a seafaring culture from northern Europe settled in the Canadian North, a claim many scholars dispute.
B204: Yesterday's Toronto is an illustrated collection edited by Linda Shapiro, offering a look at the history of Toronto. It brings together historical photographs, drawings, and writing about the city and how it grew.
B302: A Year in Provence is a 1989 memoir by Peter Mayle, a British author. He describes the first year after he and his wife bought an old farmhouse in the Luberon region of southern France, covering local characters, food, builders, and the changing seasons.
B159: Germany is a travel guide published by Dorling Kindersley, a publisher known for richly illustrated guidebooks. It covers the country's regions, cities, and sights with photographs, maps, and practical information for visitors planning a trip.
B300: Travels with Charley is a 1962 travel narrative by John Steinbeck. He tours the United States in a customized pickup camper with his poodle, Charley, and records the people and places he meets across the country.
B323: Into the Magic Shop is a 2016 memoir by James R. Doty, a neurosurgeon and Stanford professor. He describes how a magic shop and its owner helped him as a boy in a troubled household, and how the lessons later shaped his career and his work on compassion.
B047: Travels with Lizbeth is a 1993 memoir by Lars Eighner, an American writer who lived on the streets of Austin and Los Angeles for several years. He writes about life with his dog, Lizbeth, and about scavenging, shelter, and survival.
B106: Das große Katzenbuch is a German-language book about cats. It appears to be a general illustrated volume that covers cat breeds, behavior, and care, though the author and edition are not identified here.
B153: You Are Here is a 2014 book by the Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield. It presents photographs he took of Earth from the International Space Station, with captions that describe the places and what they show.
B007: Stupid White Men is a 2001 book by the American filmmaker Michael Moore, subtitled and Other Sorry Excuses for the State of the Nation. It offers a satirical and political critique of the Bush administration, corporate power, and American society.
B197: The Way of Zen is a 1957 book by Alan Watts that introduces Zen Buddhism to Western readers. It covers the history of the tradition from India and China to Japan, and explains its main ideas and practices.
B121: Instant is a 2012 history of the Polaroid Corporation by Christopher Bonanos. It follows Edwin Land, the company's founder, and traces the development of instant photography, its cultural impact, and the company's decline.
B285: Smartcuts is a 2014 business and self-improvement book by Shane Snow. It uses case studies from startups, athletes, and artists to explain how some people and organizations progress faster than expected by changing methods and systems.
B163: 1000 Chairs is a reference book by Charlotte and Peter Fiell, design historians. It presents a catalogue of chair designs from the 19th century to the present, with photographs and short entries on designers and manufacturers.
B138: The Times History of Printing is an illustrated book on the history of printing. It is presumably a reference work that covers type, presses, and the spread of printed material.
B183: The Martha Manual is a 2013 household reference book by Martha Stewart. It gives practical advice on cooking, cleaning, organizing, gardening, and other everyday tasks, and is organized as a guide for running a home.
